newsitem.title: UK: Murdoch's UK papers may back Labour - report.
newsitem.headline: Murdoch's UK papers may back Labour - report.

text.p: The Sun and the Times newspapers might back Labour leader Tony Blair at Britain's next general election, the Financial Times said on Saturday.
"If both national dailies were to back Labour, it would provide a considerable boost to Mr Blair's election campaign," said the paper. The papers are owned by Rupert Murdoch's News International Plc.

The Sun was credited in helping defeat Labour at the last election in its fierce backing for the ruling Conservatives and dogged attacks on the opposition. Labour said the press distorted facts at the last election and sought to scare the electorate over the party's tax and spending plans.
But the Financial Times said the two British dailies -- one a broadsheet, the other a tabloid -- may both back Labour at the next election, which must be called by May.
It said the Times, in particular, was leaning towards Blair, whose party is some 20 percentage points ahead in the polls. Murdoch is currently deciding on the Sun's stance, said the paper.
"Whatever Mr Murdoch decides, Mr Blair will at the very least not face the pages of invective directed against...Labour in the run-up to the 1992 election," said the paper.
Murdoch has become increasingly close to Blair and meets the Labour leader every time he visits London, the paper said.
It said Murdoch -- who wields enormous power in the British media, which in turn wields huge power over public opinion in election campaigns -- believes the government is "tired."
His Sunday Times and News of the World are expected to remain pro-Conservative, the paper said.
